text_blocks.snippet: Residents in Central Illinois are frequently targeted by common digital, phone, and door-to-door scams, including fake text messages about unpaid tolls or traffic violations, phony online shopping sites, and door-to-door storm repair con artists. Government agencies and utility companies never text or call demanding immediate payment via gift cards or untraceable apps.

list.snippet: Fake Toll & Traffic Texts: Messages claim your license will be suspended or you owe money for unpaid tolls or traffic fines, using a link to steal your credit card data.
Online Shopping & Delivery Scams: Fake social media ads or texts claim a package needs a redelivery fee or offer popular goods at prices that are too good to be true.
Storm Chaser Contractors: Fraudsters go door-to-door after severe weather offering cheap, immediate roof or home repairs, demanding cash upfront and doing poor or no work.
Impersonation & Tech Support: Scammers call or use pop-ups pretending to be tech support, family members in trouble, or government officials demanding urgent secrecy and payment.
Do not click links: Never tap or open unfamiliar links in text messages or emails from unknown senders.

Practice the pause:
Take a moment to hang up and verify urgent claims by calling an official phone number yourself.
Check official sites: Look up government or court violations directly through official portals rather than following links provided in messages.

Use secure payment:

Pay with credit cards instead of wire transfers, cash, or crypto to retain fraud protection.
